title: Cobb Salad
subtitle: American composed salad with chicken, bacon, egg, avocado and blue cheese
excerpt: A composed American salad with everything arranged in rows over chopped cos and iceberg: sliced roast chicken, crisp bacon, boiled egg, avocado, tomato, and blue cheese, dressed with a sharp red-wine vinaigrette.
sourceNotes: The Cobb salad is traditionally attributed to Robert Cobb, owner of the Hollywood Brown Derby restaurant, who assembled the first version from leftovers around 1937. It was a signature dish at the Brown Derby for decades. The composed presentation (rows of toppings) is the defining characteristic and distinguishes it from a tossed salad.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: All components except the avocado can be prepped up to a day ahead. Add avocado just before serving to prevent browning.

content.text: Cobb salad is a big American composed salad, everything arranged in tidy rows across a bed of chopped lettuce. The combination is chicken, crisp bacon, hard-boiled egg, avocado, tomato, and crumbled blue cheese. The contrast between warm bacon and cold avocado, between the sharpness of the cheese and the richness of the egg, is what makes it work.
Arrange the toppings in rows across the plate for the classic look. Serve the dressing separately at the table and let people pour their own.

Whisk {{red-wine-vinegar}} of red wine vinegar with {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Pour in {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a steady stream, whisking to combine. Taste and adjust. Set aside.

Lower {{eggs}} eggs into boiling water. Cook for 10 minutes, then run under cold water. Peel and halve. Cook the bacon in a frying pan over medium-high heat until properly crisp. Drain on paper. Break into pieces.

Spread the shredded cos across a wide bowl or large platter. Arrange the chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, cherry tomatoes, roquefort and spring onions in rows across the top. Serve the dressing in a small jug alongside. Toss the salad at the table just before eating, or leave each diner to dress their own portion.

items.fix: Prepare avocado last, just before serving. A squeeze of lemon juice slows browning if it must be prepped ahead.

items.cause: Cooked too far ahead and covered while still warm.
items.fix: Cook bacon until very crisp. Leave uncovered to cool. Add to the salad at the last moment.
The dressing is served separately for this reason. Dress individual portions lightly; people can add more.

content.text: The Cobb salad is a Hollywood restaurant dish from the 1930s, put together from fridge leftovers. Its signature is the composed presentation: everything in rows, nothing mixed, nothing hidden. This is both practical (you can see exactly what is in it) and attractive. The combination of ingredients has barely changed in 80 years, which is a reasonable sign that it works.
